raidSayLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Javier Fall. Dry cleaner. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Carpenter's square, Mixtape, Marked Bus Map, Dispatcher's headset, Dog tags. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, som
A man, maybe 50s, with grey-streaked hair: "Nothing grows here but dirt and tents. Past the treeline — that's where the green is. That's where the food is."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

The drumbeat with no drummer stops at the treeline — pacing, unwilling. The walls end the argument. It's still out there.
🦎 "Those were CALIBRATION fauna! First drafts! The audience has NOTES! So we made BETTER ones!" (Something new is crying in the treeline.)

🌒 Dusk. They come out of the treeline in a knot — 2 of them, thin and road-worn — and stop at the edge of your firelight like they're not sure they're allowed closer. The oldest steps forward. "Nora Nair. From Emberhold." A pause. "We're asking for a fire."
The village is rattled. Everyone's jumpy — eyes on the treeline.
You don't know what that was. A dog-shaped silence at the treeline. Someone at the haven should hear about this.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

💬 Nadia pulls you aside. "I need to tell you something. Last night I... dreamed? No. I was AWAKE. And something spoke to me. Not the System — something else. It said: 'Tell the human to watch the northern treeline.' Then it was gone."
The village is rattled. Everyone's jumpy — eyes on the treeline.

📺 "Oh, you survived the AUDIENCE NOTES? Cute. We've stopped pretending these are animals now. That was the FINAL DRAFT, folks — what comes out of the treeline next was never alive the way you mean it."
(Something new is moving in the treeline. It was never an animal.)
